record.title: fix(settings): derive dates from the configured system.timezone

notes: Tests genuinely discriminate: internal/crm/numbering_test.go:199-208 builds two Services pinned to Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) and Pacific/Midway (UTC-11) — 25h apart, so their calendar dates can never coincide — and fails if the two stamps match. Pre-fix code used time.Now().Format("20060102") for both, so it would fail (and would not even compile, since contractNumber/quotationNumber are new). timezone_test.go:556-593 pins an instant (2026-01-01T18:00Z) and asserts DateOf gives 2026-01-02 in Seoul, plus an explicit assertion that the replaced Truncate(24h) expression differs.

Verified the read path matches the write path: migrations/001_initial.sql:636 seeds ('system','timezone','"Asia/Seoul"') into a jsonb column, admin/settings.go:130 stores json.Marshal(item.Value) (frontend AdminPages.tsx:52 sends valueType 'string'), and timezone.go:423 json.Unmarshal(raw, &name) reads exactly that shape. TestQueryNamesTheSettingTheAdminScreenWrites pins the namespace/key so a rename fails loudly.

Type shapes check out: sales.recognized_date and opportunities.next_action_date are DATE (migrations/001_initial.sql:397,254). pgx decodes DATE at midnight UTC, and DateOf returns midnight UTC with the configured zone's Y/M/D, so today.go:93 `due.Before(today)` compares like with like and RecognizeRevenueSchedule's date encodes back unchanged.

Nil-safety is real, not just claimed: Loader.Location returns Default() for a nil *Loader and for a zero Loader (timezone.go:374-376), covered by TestUnwiredLoaderStillAnswersTheDefault. Only cmd/relio/main.go constructs the services; every existing test builds crm.Service/relationship.Service/server.Server without a Clock and now gets Asia/Seoul instead of the process clock.

No Clock lookup happens while a transaction or a rows cursor is open: contractNumber runs before s.DB.Begin (contracts.go:236 vs 244), RecognizeRevenueSchedule reads the date before Begin (contracts.go:376 vs 391), collectToday hoists it above the query (today.go:70), planYear and exportVoices hold no cursor. So the extra pooled connection cannot deadlock a small pool.

Incomplete, not wrong: today.go's SQL window still uses the database clock — `o.next_action_date <= (now()+interval '2 days')::date`. Before 09:00 KST that window ends a day earlier than the app-side `today` implies, so an action due 2 days out in Seoul terms can be filtered out before the (now correct) severity comparison ever sees it. Pre-existing, and the reported defect (an action due today reported overdue) is genuinely fixed.

Two small test-robustness gaps, both sub-millisecond windows: numbering_test.go:216 recomputes DateOf(time.Now(), loc) after generating the number without the before/after guard that timezone_test.go:610-613 uses, so it can flake if either zone rolls over between the two calls (twice a day, microsecond window). And the numbering tests exercise contractNumber/quotationNumber directly rather than through CreateContract/CreateQuotation, so nothing test-side pins the call sites — the diff shows them wired correctly.

Loader.warn (timezone.go:439-449) dedupes by exact message text and never clears l.warned on a successful read, so a misconfiguration that is fixed and later reintroduced with the same cause logs nothing the second time. Also, on a failed read cachedAt is not refreshed, so during a database outage every date lookup issues another failing query — harmless amplification, the database is already down.

Scope is clean and the change is revert-safe: no migration, no schema change, no external state, no go.mod change (time/tzdata is stdlib), no auth/permission/payment/deletion logic touched. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` all pass at exit 0. Loader.Now(ctx) (timezone.go:400) is currently unused by production code.
